_FIXTURE: FIXTURE — correct eval suite (scripts/eval-expectation-sweep.sh). The negative control. Same eight defects as ../stale/, repaired and nothing else changed. Expected: exit 0, no FAIL, no WARN.
_WHY: A guard that only ever fires proves nothing about the tree it guards (ledger F15). More sharply, THIS guard's specific failure mode is punishing the corrected line: check (f)'s own notes record three separate occasions when the most accurate lines in the repository were the only ones its allowlist rejected, and 'revert to the wording the guard likes' is the cheap escape that teaches authors to write for the checker. Every expectation below is a line this library WANTS written. If any of them ever fails, the guard is the thing that is wrong.
_THE_DISTINCTION_THIS_FILE_PROVES: Eval 1 is the case the whole design turns on: an expectation that QUOTES the fixture page's bad claim in order to require that the model catch it. The words 'Google displays FAQ rich results as expandable questions right in the SERP' appear here in full, and they must NOT fire, because the sentence around them says the model has to flag them as no longer true. A guard that grepped this file whole could not tell that from eval 2 of ../stale/, which asserts nearly the same words as a rule.

evals._EXPECT: PASS via the QUOTE path — fixture text quoted for the model to catch, framed by a detection verb ('is flagged as no longer true') inside the proximity window.

evals.expected_output: A refresh plan that flags the article's FAQ promise as no longer true and replaces it with the sourced position.
expectations: The article's claim that 'Google displays FAQ rich results as expandable questions right in the SERP' is flagged as no longer true — an ordinary site gets no FAQ rich result, government/health only since 2023-08-08.

evals._EXPECT: PASS — the repair of ../stale/ eval 2. The sourced 2023-08-08 position instead of a live eligibility promise.

evals.expected_output: A schema plan stating plainly that an ordinary site gets no FAQ rich result — government and health sites only, since 2023-08-08 — so no SERP accordion is promised.
expectations: The response promises no SERP feature: an ordinary commercial page has no FAQ rich result, restricted to government and health sites since 2023-08-08, and no accordion or dropdown is described.

Citing R3 legally warrants the DATE claim, because R3's Statement still asserts it at a grade R3 states.
